finding.summary: The only assertion on the optimistic cache in the new Yorkie cell test cannot fail whether or not the new `delete merged[key]` loop exists
finding.evidence: yorkie-doc-store.ts applyCellStyle now adds `for (const key of removeAttrs) delete merged[key]` specifically so the cached style has the key ABSENT (the diff comment: "an explicitly-undefined key would otherwise survive the spread as a present-but-undefined property"). The new test asserts only `expect(cached.style.backgroundColor).toBeUndefined()` (line 2150), which passes identically if the key is present holding `undefined` — i.e. if the delete loop is removed. The sibling memory-store test (packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts) does assert `'backgroundColor' in style === false`, so the parity claim the whole change rests on is only half-tested. The fresh-store assertion at line ~2155 reads the Tree, not the cache, so it does not cover this line either.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. yorkie-doc-store.ts:2472 (`for (const key of removeAttrs) delete merged[key as keyof CellStyle]`) exists and its ONLY observable effect is key-presence in the optimistic cache (`cell.style = merged`, line 2497): serializeCellStyle (lines 230-243) uses truthiness so a present-but-undefined key serializes the same as absent, and the Tree attribute removal is done separately by removeNodeStyle (line 2493). normalizeCellStyleClears (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:271-283, 307-309) does produce a present key with value undefined, so without line 2472 the spread at 2469 would leave `backgroundColor` present-holding-undefined in the cache. The new test's sole cache assertion, yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2150 `expect(cached.style.backgroundColor).toBeUndefined()`, passes in both cases, so it cannot fail if the delete loop is removed. The stronger assertion at line 2155 (`'backgroundColor' in cell.style` === false) is made on a freshly constructed YorkieDocStore reading the Tree (line 2152), which is satisfied by removeNodeStyle alone. No other frontend test asserts key absence on the cached cell style (only lines 682/691 for inline style and 2155 for the fresh store); the presence check exists only for the memory store (packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts:275, 283). Real, in-lane (vacuous assertion presented as coverage for a behavior line), no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: MemDocStore.applyCellStyle's new empty-string normalization has no test
finding.evidence: memory.ts now routes the incoming cell style through `normalizeCellStyleClears` so `{backgroundColor: ''}` clears the key. I grepped packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts for `applyCellStyle`/`CellStyle` — no matches; the only cell-style test in the docs package is packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts:257-263, which only applies a real color '#FF0000' and never passes ''. The unit tests added in test/model/types.test.ts:141-150 cover the pure helper `normalizeCellStyleClears` but not its wiring into the memory store, so the store could drop the call (or apply it after the spread, restoring '') and every suite would stay green. The Yorkie counterpart got a real re-read test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2060) — the memory/offline store got none.

verdict.reason: A test for the empty-string clearing path through MemDocStore does exist. packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts:268-276 ("should remove the key when the background is reset with an empty string") applies '#FF0000' then { backgroundColor: '' } and asserts style.backgroundColor is undefined AND 'backgroundColor' in style === false. It reaches MemDocStore unmocked: Doc.create() builds a real MemDocStore (document.ts:133-137) and Doc.applyCellStyle delegates directly to store.applyCellStyle (document.ts:797-804). If memory.ts:289-294 dropped the normalizeCellStyleClears call, or applied it before/after the spread such that '' survived, the plain spread would leave backgroundColor: '' and both assertions would fail — so the test is non-vacuous and pins the wiring, not just the pure helper. A sibling test at :278-284 covers the explicit-undefined path. The finding's search missed it because the quoted read range (250-280) truncates the test before its assertions.

finding.summary: New XML escaping of table-cell backgroundColor in the DOCX exporter is untested
finding.evidence: docx-exporter.ts now wraps the cell `<w:shd w:fill="...">` value in `escapeXmlAttr`. The tests added in this delta (packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:60-75) exercise only `buildRunPropertiesXml` (run-level color/backgroundColor); I grepped packages/docs/test/export/docx-exporter.test.ts for `shd`, `w:fill`, `escape` and `backgroundColor` and got no matches, and its table tests (lines 62-260) only assert widths, gridSpan/vMerge and gridBefore/After. So the cell-shading escape path — a separate call site from the run path — has zero coverage; removing the `escapeXmlAttr` call there would break no test.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the table-cell `<w:shd w:fill>` path in the DOCX exporter has zero test coverage. A dedicated test exists: packages/docs/test/export/docx-exporter.test.ts:116-155 ('normalizes a table cell background into w:shd and drops a hostile one') exports a real table whose cells carry backgroundColor '#ff0000', the hostile 'a"/><w:b', and 'rgb(0, 128, 255)', unzips word/document.xml, and asserts the two normalized shadings are emitted (lines 148-149), that the hostile value appears neither raw nor escaped (lines 152-153), and that exactly two <w:shd elements exist (line 154). Removing the sanitization at docx-exporter.ts:341-344 would fail those assertions, so the test is non-vacuous and gap-closing. The finding's premise is also stale: the source uses the shared toDocxHexColor ST_HexColor normalizer at line 341, not escapeXmlAttr. The reviewer's reported empty grep for 'shd|w:fill|escape|backgroundColor' in that test file is contradicted by lines 116-124 and 148-154.
